summary: The top clips all lead with a single wild or quotable moment and never waste a frame on setup. The 200K cameraman clip (2,960 views) dominates because the hook text names a specific, surprising number and the subtitle echoes the spoken punchline in real time. Clips in the 1,000–1,300 view range share a physical or social-awkwardness angle (handstand, fart, flirting) that is universally relatable without needing context. Titles that pair a concrete detail with an emoji and a payoff phrase ('the excuse is crazy') outperform vague titles. Clips that stay under 25 seconds outperform longer ones; the only 43-second entry earned 2 views. Everything landing above 1,000 views uses blur-fill framing with the stream frame centered so faces read clearly on mobile.
moments_to_pick: Cartier drops a specific, surprising number or stat out loud (salary, price, count) — the more specific the better
A stranger physically interacts with Cartier or crew in an unexpected way (challenge, skill demo, confrontation)
An unscripted social moment goes sideways — flirting, rejection, an awkward reveal
Chat or someone nearby says or does something Cartier visibly reacts to with shock or laughter
A one-liner or made-up word Cartier coins that sounds quotable out of context
An embarrassing or gross physical moment someone in the stream tries to explain away
hook_examples: He said WHAT about the job? 💀
Bro tried to teach himself this in 60 seconds
She didn't know the camera was still on 😭
He got caught lacking on live fr
The excuse after this is WILD 😂
Chat went crazy when he said this 💀
title_formula: Lead with who did what in plain English, include one specific surprising detail (a number, a word, a reaction), end with a 1–4 word payoff phrase or question, add one relevant emoji. Format: [Specific thing that happened] and [the wild detail/consequence] [emoji]. Keep under 70 characters. Example:
caption_formula: Line 1: One punchy sentence that rewords the hook — do not repeat the title word for word. Line 2: A second sentence that teases the payoff without spoiling it, written as Cartier's voice or perspective. Line 3: 'Catch Cartier live on Kick: kick.com/cartier2real'. Keep total under 3 lines visible be
avoid: Any slow intro or establishing shot before the punchline moment — cut straight to the moment
Clips longer than 25 seconds unless the moment physically cannot be understood shorter
Vague titles with no concrete detail ('Cartier reacts to something crazy') — always name the thing
Currency symbols anywhere in titles, captions or on-screen text (campaign rule)
On-screen hook text that is ALL CAPS shouting — sentence case reads better for the hook banner based on the top clip thumbnail
Reusing the exact same emoji in both the title and the hook text — vary them
experiment: On one clip this cycle, put a bold numerical stat or dollar amount as the very first on-screen text (e.g. '200K A YEAR' in the top bar before any subtitle appears) to replicate the exact visual pattern of the highest-performing clip and test whether that element alone lifts watch time past the 2-sec
our_results_note: No posts yet from this channel — all benchmarks are drawn from the campaign's existing clips. Prioritise the 200K cameraman clip's formula (specific number + on-screen echo of the spoken line) as the baseline to beat.
